summary: Enhance your skills in water loss and non-revenue water management with our comprehensive training course. Join us to optimize resources and reduce waste.
lede: Non-revenue water management helps water-system professionals account for water losses and unbilled authorized consumption. For utility managers, operators, and specialists, the course covers quantifying losses, locating leaks, managing pressure, and improving meter and billing accuracy. Learners also practice using water-audit data to set reduction targets and build an operational plan for monitoring progress.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage water systems, reduce operational waste, and recover revenue through strategic NRW control. It targets hands-on practitioners, managers, specialists, and leaders who must deliver measurable reductions in water loss under real-world constraints. Whether you’re managing a city-wide network, running a rural water board, or implementing an NGO-funded project, this training equips you to turn scattered knowledge into a credible, operational system. The course is designed for: Utility Manager:
audience: Oversee city-wide NRW reduction programs and report
NRW Specialist: Conduct water audits, quantify losses
Operations Engineer: Implement leak detection programs, pressure
Asset Planner: Assess infrastructure conditions, plan long-term
Billing Supervisor: Eliminate apparent losses through meter
Hydraulic Modeler: Use EPANET to optimize pressure
GIS Analyst: Map leak detection data, integrate
Customer Engagement Coordinator: Design conservation programs, manage
Financial Analyst: Build business cases for NRW
modules: Foundations of Non-Revenue Water and Loss Classification
Leak Detection Technologies and Proactive Leakage Management
Pressure Management for Real Loss Reduction
Smart Metering and Apparent Loss Elimination
Infrastructure Assessment and Long-Term Rehabilitation Planning
Customer Engagement and Commercial Loss Control
Regulatory Compliance and Financial Justification for NRW Programs
Integrated NRW Reduction Strategy and Implementation Roadmap
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of utility operations (production flow, customer metering, pressure logs) and basic Excel skills. No coding or advanced hydraulics required. Pre-course prep: Review the IWA Water Balance diagram and AWWA M36 summary (links provided in course portal). If you manage utility data or operations, you’re ready; if you’re new to utilities, take a foundational water utility course first.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
